newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks tumble amid profit-taking, Dow woes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks tumble amid profit-taking, Dow woes.

text.p: Mexican stocks tumbled Friday as jitters over a sharp slide on Wall Street spurred profit-taking, analysts and dealers said.

"Market volatility increased and mirrored movements in the Dow Jones. Still, players in the bourse took profits on low volume and the market still looks solid," said Alexander Anderson, reasearch head at the Abaco brokerage.
The leading IPC share index fell 120.24 points, or 2.31 percent, to 5,075.05. Trading volume was moderate at 89.1 million shares.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 156.78 points to 8,031.22 and the 30-year U.S. Treasury fell 1-7/16, or $14.38 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.64 percent from 6.53 percent Thursday.
Profit-taking on Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) and Bancomer, which accounted for one-third of all shares traded, weighed most on the market, dealers said.

Telmex fell 60 centavos (8 cents) to 21.90 pesos ($2.80) as its American Depositary Receipts shed 1-3/8 to 53-13/16. Financial firm Bancomer A shares ended down 15 centavos (2 cents) to 3.60 pesos (46 cents).
Financial stocks fell amid concerns that higher interest rates would worsen past-due loan problems, dealers said.
Of the 36 stocks that make up the IPC, just two ended with gains -- steelmaker Altos Hornos de Mexico and corn flour and tortilla supplier Maseca.
"Ahmsa had lagged the market a little, and as for Maseca, selling tortillas is always good business in Mexico," a dealer said.
Ahmsa gained 15 centavos (2 cents) to 21.40 pesos ($2.74), while Maseca ended up six centavos (less than 1 cent) to 9.36 pesos ($1.20).

Accel was the most active stock elsewhere, rising 10 centavos (1 cent) to 2.17 pesos (28 cents). Traders said the holding company was a market straggler that was still reaping the benefits of a recommendation made on Wednesday.
On the broad market, decliners outnumbered gainers, 74-20.
